senses.definition: One of two babies who began from the same fertilized egg and usually have very similar DNA.
senses.example: An identical twin can have likes and interests that differ from the other twin’s.

senses.definition: A group of words that means something different as a group from what the separate words might suggest.
senses.example: In the idiom “piece of cake,” the speaker means a task was easy.

senses.definition: Rock made when melted material cools and becomes solid.
senses.example: Obsidian is an igneous rock that can have a glassy surface.

senses.definition: A drawing or picture that shows something from a story or helps explain a subject.
senses.example: The illustration showed what Peter Rabbit saw in the garden.

senses.definition: The amount of picture detail a grid can store, often described by how many pixels it has across and down.
senses.example: The image resolution is 300 pixels across and 200 pixels tall.

senses.definition: A person who comes to live in another country.
senses.example: The museum keeps records of immigrants who sailed into New York Harbor.

senses.definition: Making up part of a performance as you do it.
senses.example: The trumpet player used improvisation to change the end of the tune.

senses.definition: Something you pay for from inside a game or other app.
senses.example: We check with an adult before making an in-app purchase.

senses.definition: A front tooth with a sharp edge used for cutting into food.
senses.example: An incisor cut off a small piece of apple.

senses.definition: An organized set of clues that helps someone or something find information quickly.
senses.example: The search engine checked an index for pages about boats.

senses.definition: In chemistry, a substance that shows something about a liquid, often by changing color.
senses.example: A pH indicator can change from purple to pink in an acidic drink.

senses.definition: A kind of light that human eyes cannot see. Warm things often give off infrared light.
senses.example: Webb can collect infrared light from a cloud of dust.

senses.definition: To get a feature or piece of genetic information from biological parents.
senses.example: Children inherit different mixes of DNA.

senses.definition: The part of the ear farthest from the outside that contains organs for hearing and balance.
senses.example: The inner ear sends clues about head movement to the brain.

senses.definition: One part of a baseball game in which each team has a turn to bat.
senses.example: Both teams scored in the third inning.

senses.definition: A number, fact, or signal you give to a rule, device, or system.
senses.example: In a number machine that adds two, an input of three gives five.

senses.definition: Words or signs written, stamped, or cut onto a surface, such as stone, metal, or paper.
senses.example: The inscription on the statue’s base told us who it showed.

senses.definition: The worldwide system that connects many networks and lets computers exchange information.
senses.example: I can use the internet to send a message to someone far away.

senses.definition: A long, folded tube in the body that helps take useful parts from food and carry along the rest.
senses.example: Your small intestine takes in most nutrients.

senses.definition: The colored ring in an eye that changes the size of the opening in its center.
senses.example: Her iris is brown.

senses.definition: An element that can be a metal and is also needed in tiny forms by the body to help carry oxygen.
senses.example: The beans in my lunch provide some iron.

senses.definition: Bringing water to land or plants with pipes, channels, or other equipment, especially when rain alone is not enough.
senses.example: The farm uses drip irrigation to send water to the roots of the plants.

senses.definition: A narrow strip of land that joins two larger areas of land, with water on both sides.
senses.example: The Isthmus of Panama connects the land of Central and South America.
